Myrtle Beach is the largest city on the Grand Strand and one of the most popular tourist destinations on the East Coast, drawing approximately 20 million visitors annually. This massive influx of visitors — most of whom are unfamiliar with local roads — combined with a permanent population of roughly 43,000 creates extremely dangerous driving conditions, particularly along US-17 (Kings Highway) and Highway 501.

Horry County had the second-highest rate of fatal crashes of any county in South Carolina in 2022, with 78 fatal collisions resulting in 80 deaths. US-17 through Myrtle Beach is designated as a high-crash corridor by the South Carolina Department of Public Safety. Roden Law’s Murrells Inlet office at 631 Bellamy Ave. serves all of Myrtle Beach. If you’ve been injured in an accident, call (843) 612-1980 for a free case review.

Darien is the county seat of McIntosh County and home to Roden Law's Georgia coastal office at 1108 North Way. With approximately 1,500 city residents and 11,000 countywide, Darien is a historic shrimping community situated at the mouth of the Altamaha River — one of the largest undammed rivers on the East Coast. The city is also home to Fort King George, the oldest English fort on the Georgia coast, dating to 1721.

Despite its small size, Darien sits directly on Interstate 95 and US-17, placing it in the path of massive commercial truck traffic volumes traveling between Savannah and Jacksonville. The rural stretches of I-95 through McIntosh County are particularly dangerous during nighttime and early morning hours, when fatigued truckers pass through with minimal lighting and few rest facilities. Boating accidents on the Altamaha River and surrounding intracoastal waterways also affect McIntosh County residents. As Darien's local personal injury law firm, Roden Law is deeply connected to this community. Call (912) 303-5850 for a free case review.

_roden_neighborhood_roads: Interstate 95 through McIntosh County between Exits 49 and 58 is a high-speed corridor where commercial tractor-trailer crashes are common, particularly during early morning hours when fatigued long-haul truckers pass through the rural stretch between Savannah and Brunswick. US-17 (Ocean Highway) through Darien crosses the Altamaha River on a bridge that creates dangerous conditions during fog — the Altamaha River bridge approach is a known accident site where rear-end collisions occur when vehicles suddenly slow for the bridge in low-visibility conditions. GA-251 connects I-95 to Darien proper and carries traffic through a narrow corridor with limited shoulders and residential driveways that create turning conflicts. The I-95/GA-251 interchange (Exit 49) is a critical merge point where commercial traffic conflicts with local traffic heading to the Darien waterfront, shrimp docks, and Fort King George. Timber trucks traveling from interior McIntosh County to the coast use narrow county roads not designed for their weight and size.
